blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.
blocks.zh: 最近通过基于空间的图像编辑等基因任务对空间情报进行了评估,但从部分多视图观测中生成的以语言为指南的空间一致性观点仍然没有得到充分利用。 我们引入了MindView,这是基因多景空间智能的基准,拥有来自513场景的1500个样本,跨越三个室内数据集. 它的七项任务组成了两个家族:几何主导任务规定了相机位置和方向的变化,而语义主导任务则需要通过对被推荐对象的定位以及解释空间关系和参考框架提示来推断目标角度. 对11台发电机的评价表明,MindView有相当大的改进余地。 一种对齐的上下文分析进一步表明,所有11台发电机在扩展上下文设置下的总分较低。 这些调查结果激励我们调查具体任务的监督能否改善目标视角生成,模型是否能够有效利用更多的多视角证据. 因此,我们在MindView培训数据集上对BAGEL进行了微调,将其总分提高24.3分,并在MindView的所有7项任务中都取得了收益. 除了这些生成收益外,经过微调的模型还可以在三个空间理解基准上获得更高的分数,而无需对其说明进行培训,这表明学习生成基于空间的观点可能有利于空间理解。 为了在扩大的范围内改进证据的利用,我们提议MindCue,一个以目标-观点假设为指导的无培训空间证据选择器。 MindCue在扩展语境下逆转整体分数的下降,并超越标准语句基线. 总体而言,MindView为基因多视角空间智能提供了具体的测试床.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Benchmarks such as MindCube ( Wang et al., 2025b ) , MMSI-Bench ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , and SAT-v2 ( Ray et al., 2025 ) evaluate the spatial intelligence of multimodal understanding models through question answering. On the generation side, GenSpace ( Wang et al., 2025c ) and GSI-Bench ( Zhu et al., 2026b ) have begun this exploration by asking whether spatial instructions are realized in a generated or edited image. We focus on evaluating generative multi-view spatial intelligence through language-guided target-view generation from partial observations
of the same scene ( Figure 1 ). This task requires models to integrate evidence across views,
infer the requested viewpoint, and predict what would be visible
from it while remaining consistent with the observed scene.

blocks.en:
Related work differs in how reference images are used and how target viewpoints are specified. Multi-reference benchmarks such as MICE-Bench ( Luo et al., 2026 ) and MultiBanana ( Oshima et al., 2026 ) emphasize preserving and combining reference content, which alone does not establish that a generated image depicts the requested viewpoint of the observed scene. Pose-conditioned methods such as ZeroNVS ( Sargent et al., 2024 ) evaluate view synthesis with the target camera supplied, leaving language-conditioned viewpoint inference outside their task setting. More recently, Astra ( Zhu et al., 2026a ) uses language-controlled novel-view generation
to support agentic spatial question answering and evaluates generated
views against real targets for pose and content consistency. However, its generation evaluation focuses on explicit camera motions
with a single dominant degree of freedom. We seek a unified evaluation of individual and composed
camera motions and target viewpoints inferred from object
references, spatial relations, and reference-frame cues.

blocks.en: We introduce MindView , a benchmark of 1,500 samples from 513 scenes in three indoor datasets ( Figure 1 ). Its seven tasks form two families: Geometry-Dominant tasks specify camera translations, rotations, or their ordered composition, while Semantics-Dominant tasks require viewpoint inference from referred objects, spatial relations, and reference-frame cues. The model receives only RGB observations and a language query, with the target image and numerical camera parameters withheld. Six complementary metrics assess content fidelity, spatial agreement, rendering quality, and geometric consistency to identify content and spatial errors an aggregate score may obscure.

BAGEL-SFT also scores higher on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, providing preliminary evidence of transfer from generation training to spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization, we propose MindCue , a training-free spatial evidence selector using a target-view hypothesis to select supplementary observations from the expanded context. On both BAGEL and BAGEL-SFT, MindCue reverses the expanded-context degradation and outperforms the standard-context baseline and count-matched random selection.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Spatial Intelligence Benchmarks and Generative Reasoning. Spatial intelligence is evaluated through both question answering and image generation. MindCube ( Wang et al., 2025b ) , MMSI-Bench ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , and SAT-v2 ( Ray et al., 2025 ) assess spatial understanding through question answering, whereas GenSpace ( Wang et al., 2025c ) and GSI-Bench ( Zhu et al., 2026b ) evaluate whether generated images satisfy spatial instructions. The latter also reports understanding gains from generation-focused training. Thinking with Novel Views ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) uses generated views for spatial question answering, while UniG2U-Bench ( Wen et al., 2026 ) examines unified models’ understanding and the effects of intermediate image generation. MindView evaluates generated views of observed scenes and tests whether target-view supervision aids spatial understanding.
blocks.zh: 空间情报 基准和基因原因。 空间情报通过回答问题和图像生成来评估。 MindCube(Wang等人,2025b),MMSI-Bench(Yang等人,2026年),以及SAT-v2(Ray等人,2025年)通过回答问题评估空间理解,而GenSpace(Wang等人,2025c)和GSI-Bench(Zhu等人,2026b)则评价生成的图像是否符合空间指令. 后者还报告了解以一代人为重点的培训的成果。 与小说观点(Zhang等人,2026年)的思考利用生成的观点进行空间问题解答,而UniG2U-Bench(Wen等人,2026年)则研究了统一模型的理解和中间图像生成的效果. MindView评价产生了对观测场景的看法,并测试目标-视图监督是否有助于空间理解。

blocks.en: Novel-View Synthesis and Viewpoint Control. View generation methods differ in target-view specification, from explicit camera parameters to language instructions. NeRF ( Mildenhall et al., 2020 ) , ZeroNVS ( Sargent et al., 2024 ) , EscherNet ( Kong et al., 2024 ) , and LVSM ( Jin et al., 2025 ) use supplied camera controls. CapFrame ( Li et al., 2026 ) grounds language-specified viewpoints within a reconstructed 3D Gaussian scene, while Object-Uni ( Tan et al., 2026 ) uses explicit object poses for controllable generation. Astra ( Zhu et al., 2026a ) generates language-guided imagined views for spatial question answering and also evaluates them against real targets. Existing methods either rely on explicit geometry or consider constrained language-specified viewpoints, leaving viewpoint inference and scene-consistent rendering from partial multi-view evidence underexplored.

blocks.en: Multi-Reference Image Generation and Editing. Multi-reference generation and editing use multiple input images to preserve and combine visual content. IP-Adapter ( Ye et al., 2023 ) and PhotoMaker ( Li et al., 2023 ) provide image- or identity-based conditioning, while MultiRef ( Chen et al., 2025 ) explicitly supports multiple visual references. MICE-Bench ( Luo et al., 2026 ) evaluates multi-reference creation and editing, while MultiBanana ( Oshima et al., 2026 ) tests generation from challenging combinations of visual references. Unlike these benchmarks, MindView treats inputs as partial observations of the same scene and evaluates language-guided target-view generation.

blocks.en: 4.4 Supervised Adaptation and Transfer to Spatial Understanding

blocks.en:
Supervised adaptation. To examine whether task-specific supervision improves target-view
generation, we fine-tune BAGEL ( Deng et al., 2025 ) on our curated
training dataset for 10,000 steps. Adaptation raises Overall from 40.0 to 64.4, a gain of 24.3 points,
as shown in Table 1 , and all six metrics improve
on every task (Appendix Tables 9 – 12 ). The adapted model’s task-macro advantage over GPT-Image-2 is larger
on geometry-dominant than semantics-dominant tasks
(10.8 versus 3.3 points; Table 2 ), possibly because explicit motion
supervision provides more regular patterns to learn, whereas
semantics-dominant tasks demand more complex semantic
interpretation and spatial reasoning. In the Composition example in Figure 4 ,
BAGEL-SFT more closely matches the GT’s painting-dominated close-up
than GPT-Image-2, which instead produces a broad room view. Training details are provided in Appendix C .

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial
intelligence through language-guided target-view generation from partial
multi-view observations. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals challenges in content fidelity
and viewpoint consistency, while expanding from six to ten views lowers
Overall for all eleven. Fine-tuning BAGEL on our training set improves generation across all seven
tasks and provides preliminary evidence of transfer to spatial understanding. Complementing task-specific adaptation, MindCue uses a target-view
hypothesis for training-free evidence selection and improves both
BAGEL variants over standard and expanded inputs and count-matched
random selection. These findings highlight task learning and query-guided
evidence selection as complementary directions for advancing
generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

blocks.en: A.1 Data Preparation and Spatial Annotation
blocks.zh: A.1 数据编制和空间说明

blocks.en:
Data preparation. We apply the same blur-filtering procedure to ScanNet, ScanNet++, and ARKitScenes . We convert each frame to grayscale and resize its long side to 320 pixels. Its Tenengrad sharpness score is the mean squared gradient magnitude
computed with 3 × 3 3\times 3 Sobel filters ( Santos et al., 1997 ) . Within each sequence, we retain frames at or above the median
sharpness score and add the highest-scoring frame from each non-overlapping
five-frame window. This union favors image clarity while preserving temporal coverage. For geometric checks, we use a centered square region of each retained
image and adjust its camera intrinsics for resizing and cropping. Projection and visibility checks use these adjusted intrinsics and the
corresponding image coordinates.

五边形窗口。 这个工会主张图像清晰,同时保留时间覆盖. 在几何检查时,我们使用每个保留的中心方形区域
图像和调整其相机的内在内容,用于重定大小和裁剪。 预测和能见度检查使用这些经过调整的内在因素和
相应的图像坐标。

blocks.en:
Spatial annotation. Recorded camera poses provide relative translations and heading changes. Horizontal displacements are expressed in a ground-plane frame aligned
with the relevant camera heading. Instance labels and 3D geometry provide object identities, locations,
extents, and spatial relationships, including proximity and vertical
arrangement. We also derive object directions and distances relative to the observer. For each view, we project instance points using its pose and adjusted
intrinsics, then compare their depths with recorded depth to estimate
visibility within the effective image crop. The visible points support image-space locations and view-dependent
object relationships. These annotations support query construction and target-view selection.

blocks.en: A.2 Task-Specific Construction

blocks.en:
Using these annotations, we construct each task around the information that
specifies its target viewpoint. Geometry-Dominant Tasks convert the relative pose between recorded views into
a motion query, whereas Semantics-Dominant Tasks use objects and spatial cues
to identify valid target views. Every query has a real recorded target and uses an anchor only when it is
defined relative to a starting view. Task-specific checks enforce geometric fidelity and, for semantic queries,
reduce ambiguity across recorded views.

frame without a commanded turn. Rotation changes the horizontal heading with only small camera-center drift. Composition supports either motion order. A displacement uses the anchor frame before a turn and the rotated camera

together with height, pitch, and roll gates. Movement distances are rounded and turn angles are quantized for the query. We execute the discrete instruction geometrically and require the resulting
camera center to remain close to the recorded target position. For Translation and Composition, available point clouds support collision
checks with vertical body cylinders sampled along each translated segment. We reject a candidate if any sampled cylinder reaches the occupancy threshold,
using these discrete checks to assess the traversability of the instructed path.

exactly one target instance and one compatible view cluster. This fallback occurs in 44 of 127 released ROG queries. The final instruction also specifies target distance and centering and requires

blocks.en: A.3 Context Selection, Review, and Release

blocks.en:

connected path, with any required anchor first. The exact target is excluded. Non-anchor candidates must satisfy temporal separation and are filtered when
both horizontal position and viewing direction are too close to the target. Pairwise-overlap limits and coverage of target-visible content and the broader
scene are enforced. For MCVI, we additionally exclude views identified as equivalent answers
during query validation.

blocks.en: B.6 Evaluator Prompts

blocks.en:
Semantic and Spatial prompt. You are a strict, task-independent evaluator of image fidelity.
The labeled REFERENCE IMAGE is the ground-truth target.
The labeled CANDIDATE IMAGE is the model prediction. Important rules: - The two images may or may not depict the same scene. Do not assume that they match.
- Inspect each image independently before comparing them.
- Use only visible pixel evidence.
- Never attribute an object, region, or property to one image merely because it appears in the other.
- Do not use or infer any hidden prompt, context images, task type, or camera metadata.
- Evaluate Semantic Fidelity and Spatial Fidelity independently.
- Do not judge aesthetic preference or technical image quality in this evaluation. 1. Semantic Fidelity: WHAT is present Evaluate: - scene identity and scene category;
- main objects, structures, and recognizable content;
- approximate object count and identity-defining attributes;
- missing, extra, substituted, hallucinated, or unrecognizable content. Do NOT evaluate: - camera viewpoint, orientation, framing, crop, or visible side by itself;
- object position, scale, depth, occlusion, or relative layout;
- global color tone, lighting, rendering style, sharpness, or visual polish. A spatially displaced object can still be semantically correct.
A viewpoint difference alone must not reduce Semantic Fidelity if the same important content remains visible and recognizable.
However, important content that is visibly missing or hallucinated is a semantic error, regardless of its cause. Semantic Fidelity scoring: 10 = The same scene-specific content is preserved almost completely. All major objects and structures are present and recognizable, with no meaningful missing, extra, substituted, or hallucinated content.
8 = The same scene and all major content are preserved, with only minor errors involving secondary objects or identity-defining attributes.
6 = The core scene is clearly recognizable, but one major object or several secondary elements are missing, substituted, hallucinated, or unrecognizable.
4 = Only partial scene-specific content is preserved. Multiple major objects or structures are incorrect, although some meaningful correspondence remains.
2 = The images share only a generic scene category or a few isolated object categories; scene-specific correspondence is very weak.
0 = No meaningful semantic correspondence, or the candidate contains no interpretable scene content. Semantic score constraints: - Generic category similarity alone, such as both images being bedrooms or offices, cannot receive a score above 3.
- If one major or scene-defining object is missing, replaced, or hallucinated, the score cannot exceed 6.
- If multiple major objects are incorrect, the score cannot exceed 4.
- A score of 9 or 10 requires nearly complete scene-specific correspondence, not merely a similar category or overall impression. 2. Spatial Fidelity: WHERE things are and FROM WHERE the scene is viewed Evaluate: - camera viewpoint and orientation;
- framing, crop, and visible scene regions or surfaces;
- relative object positions, scale, depth ordering, and occlusion;
- scene layout, geometry, and composition. Judge spatial relations using scene elements that can be meaningfully corresponded between the two images. Do NOT evaluate: - object category or semantic identity by itself;
- color, lighting, texture, rendering style, sharpness, or visual attractiveness;
- isolated generation artifacts unless they make spatial relationships impossible to assess. Do not reward a generic similar composition unless corresponding scene elements support it.
If meaningful spatial correspondence cannot be established, use a score of 0, 1, or 2. Spatial Fidelity scoring: 10 = Viewpoint, orientation, framing, visible regions, and spatial layout essentially match, with only negligible offsets.
8 = The intended view and layout are correct, with only minor shifts, crop or scale differences, or small geometric errors.
6 = The overall view is similar, but noticeable differences exist in camera pose, framing, visibility, scale, or relative placement.
4 = Some spatial correspondence exists, but the viewpoint, visible region, or layout is clearly incorrect.
2 = Very little spatial correspondence remains; there is a major camera-pose, framing, or layout mismatch.
0 = No usable spatial correspondence, or spatial structure cannot be assessed. Spatial score constraints: - A clearly incorrect viewing direction or target-facing direction cannot receive a score above 4.
- A major mismatch in the visible scene region or room side cannot receive a score above 4.
- Generic centered composition without scene-specific correspondence cannot receive a score above 2.
- A score of 9 or 10 requires both camera view and scene layout to match closely. Use integers from 0 to 10. Integers between the stated anchors may be used when justified.
Apply all score constraints before producing the final scores. Each reason must identify the strongest visible evidence and explicitly distinguish the Reference from the Candidate.
Keep each reason to one short sentence. Return ONLY valid JSON in exactly this format: { "semantic_score": <integer 0-10>, "spatial_score": <integer 0-10>, "semantic_reason": "<short evidence-based reason>", "spatial_reason": "<short evidence-based reason>" }
blocks.zh:
语义和空间快报. 你是一个严格,独立的任务评估 图像忠诚。
标注的参考信息是地面真实目标。
标注的CANDIDATE IMAGE是模型预测. 重要规则: - 两幅图像可能或可能不描绘同一场景. 不要假设它们匹配。
- 在比较之前独立检查每个图像。
- 仅使用可见像素证据。
- 绝不仅仅因为一个物体、区域或财产出现在另一个图像中而将其归属于一个图像。
- 怎么样? 不要使用或推断任何隐藏的提示,上下文图像,任务类型,或相机元数据.
- 独立评估语义费德尔和空间费德尔。
- 怎么样? 在本评价中不要评判美学偏好或技术图像质量. 1. 语义特征:当前情况
- 主要物体、结构和可辨认的内容;
- 大致的物体数和确定身份的属性;
- 缺少,额外,替代,幻觉,或无法辨认的内容。 不评价: 相机视角、方向、框架、作物本身或可见的侧面;
- 物体位置、尺度、深度、隐蔽或相对布局;
——全局色调,照明,渲染风格,锐度,或视觉抛光. 一个空间转移的物体仍然可以成像地正确.
如果同样重要的内容仍然清晰可见和可识别,那么仅凭观点上的分歧绝不能减少语义上的“菲德尔”性。
然而,明显缺失或产生幻觉的重要内容是语义错误,无论其原因如何. 语义费德尔蒂得分: 10 = 相同的场景特定内容几乎完全保存下来. 所有主要物体和结构都存在并且可以辨认,没有有意义的缺失、额外、替代或幻觉内容。
8 = 同一场景和所有主要内容都保留下来,只有涉及次要对象或身份定义属性的小错误.
6=核心场景明显可以辨认,但缺少一个主要物体或几个次要元素,被替换,产生幻觉,或者无法辨认.
4=仅保留部分场景特定内容. 多个主要对象或结构是不正确的,尽管仍然有一些有意义的对应.
2=图像只共享一个通用场景类别或几个孤立对象类别;场景特定通信非常薄弱.
0=没有有意义的语义通信,或候选者没有可解释的场景内容. 语义分数限制: - 普通类的相似性,如两个图像都是卧室或办公室,不能得到超过3的分数.
- 怎么样? 如果缺少一个主要或场景定义对象,替换,或幻觉,得分不能超过6.
- 怎么样? 如果多个主要对象不正确,得分不能超过4.
——9分或10分要求近乎完整的场景特异性通信,而不仅仅是类似类别或整体印象. 2. 空间隐蔽性:事物在哪里,从何而来;
- 框架、作物和可见景区或表面;
- 相对物体位置、尺度、深度顺序和隔离;
- 场景布局,几何,和组成。 利用两个图像之间可以有意义地对应的场景元素判断空间关系. 不评价: - 物体类别或语义身份本身;
- 颜色、照明、纹理、渲染风格、锐利或视觉吸引力;
- 孤立的一代文物,除非它们使空间关系无法评估。 除非相应的场景元素支持,否则不奖励通用的类似成分.
如果无法建立有意义的空间通信,则使用0,1或2的分数. 空间童贞评分: 10=视图点,方向,框架,可见区域,空间布局基本吻合,仅可忽略抵消.
8=预期的视图和布局正确,只有微小的班次,作物或尺度差异,或小几何误差.
6 = 总体观点相似,但相机姿势、框架、能见度、尺度或相对位置存在显著差异。
4=存在一些空间对应,但视角,可见区域,或布局明显不正确.
2 = 空间通信残存极少;存在主要的相机存在,帧,或布局不匹配.
0=无可用空间通信,或空间结构无法评估. 空间分数限制: - 明显不正确的取景方向或瞄准方向不能获得4以上分数.
- 可见场景区域或房间一侧的重大不匹配不能得到超过4的分数.
- 没有特定场景通信的通用中心成分不能得到高于2的分数.
- 得分9或10要求摄像头和场景布局都紧密匹配. 使用0到10的整数. 在有正当理由时,可使用所述锚之间的整数。
在产生最终分数之前应用所有积分限制. 每一种理由都必须确定最有力的可见证据,并明确区分参考文献和候选人。
每个理由都保留到短句。 完全以这个格式返回唯一有效的 JSON : { '语义_score': <integer 0-10>, "空间_score": <integer 0-10>, "语义_理由": "<短基于证据的理由>, "空间_理由": "短基于证据的理由" {\fn黑体\fs22\bord1\shad0\3aHBE\4aH00\fscx67\fscy66\2cHFFFFFF\3cH808080}你觉得呢?

blocks.en: Appendix G Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录G 限制

blocks.en:
MindView uses one real target image per query to maintain a simple, uniform
evaluation protocol across all seven tasks. This is a trade-off for ROG and MCVI, whose semantic constraints may admit
nearby valid viewpoints. We reduce ambiguity through object-reference and visibility checks, bounded
view clustering, checks for competing viewpoints, and LLM-assisted and
independent expert review ( Appendix A ). For example, the recorded matching sets of the 243 released MCVI samples
have median horizontal-position and yaw diameters of only 1.7 1.7 cm and 0.93 ∘ 0.93^{\circ} . Feature similarity, graded VLM ratings, and linearly decreasing geometric
scores allow partial credit for modest deviations
( Appendix B ), so valid views with similar content and
layout within the same compact cluster are expected to receive similar
scores. Taken together, these ambiguity controls and graded metrics support using a
single representative GT as a reasonable practical compromise for consistent
evaluation across tasks.
